python.commit_subject: docs(audit): 工具契约深度审计（Python 857/270 vs Go 137；Skill 25/25 逐字一致）
python.note: capture ran at 1b9c458a; core/ is unchanged since a756b1e5 and the tool/queen sources since 68b6c230, so the captured surface is identical at both commits

captures.method: fake OpenAI-compatible gateway in front of each runtime's `serve`; llm.api_base pointed at it; create a queen session; POST one chat message; record the request body verbatim

python.home: temporary HIVE_HOME, no credentials, clean queens/ tree

go_catalogue_union.difference: 147 - 4 colony-only tools (get_worker_status, inject_message, run_worker, stop_worker) + 1 synthetic (ask_user) = 144

source_level_audit.note: static source scan (Python 857 all / 270 default tools, Go 137 session tools); this manifest is the runtime-captured LLM layer and agrees with go_session_tools=137

uncovered: Python colony/worker tool surfaces (worker sessions, colony overseer) — only the default independent-phase DM queen session was captured.

Python deferred (searchable) tool schemas: they never reach the request. Names appear only in the user turn's <system-reminder>; this capture listed chart_render and web_scrape (the email_senders category is hidden while the feature flag is off).

Go MCP-origin tools: with a clean HIVE_HOME the Go runtime registers no MCP server (mcp_servers=[], stale=true), so its whole LLM surface comes from the builtin catalogue. The MCP catalog layer has no Go counterpart to compare against.
Credentialed (OAuth) integration tools on the Python side: connected_providers=[] in a clean home, so gmail/github/hubspot/... are in neither the catalog nor the request.
Output/return schemas: neither runtime declares one in the tool definition (the source audit also reports py_output_schema=0).
Anthropic Messages protocol path: only the OpenAI-compatible serialization was captured.
System-prompt coupling: the Python <searchable_tools>/<system-reminder> manifest was captured; Go sends no equivalent block because nothing is deferred.

tool_library_layer.note: Python's allowlist names 25 tools but only 13 are in the live MCP catalog and 12 are deferred/in-process; the Go snapshot names 24 because it has no MCP catalog to enumerate in a clean home

recheck.result: LLM-visible tool surface unchanged: the window only touched core/framework/agent_loop (memory_reminders etc.), tools/src/memory_tools, tools/src/terminal_tools and version files; no core/framework/tools, no tools/src/aden_tools/tools/** or aden_tools/credentials changes. Tool contract at version 1.0.15 therefore equals the 1.0.14 capture; a re-capture run is only required when a future upstream window touches tool defs.
